title: Migrate v1 artifact names to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant

facts.note: Contextual cue only: task keywords alone do not activate this rule; a legacy v1 name must actually be the subject of migration (see finding).
Contextual cue only: files that carry artifact names, URNs or $id fields; file kind alone does not activate this rule.
Required predicate: a detector recognising names lacking a theme prefix or using dots for hierarchy (v1 shape).
Diff-level observer for a v1 name being rewritten to v2 in names / URNs / $id values.

fires: A plan or wagon task migrates a legacy v1 name such as identifiers:uuid or ux.foundations.color to the v2 pattern.
A planner migrates a legacy v1 artifact name to v2 and must update the wagon manifest, feature files, URNs, contract layout and $id fields that carry it.
A legacy v1 name with no theme prefix is found while authoring a new wagon or acceptance and is to be migrated.
doesNotFire: Authoring a brand-new artifact name with no legacy v1 predecessor (the naming-pattern convention governs that).
Renaming an artifact whose name is already in v2 theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant form (an ordinary rename, not a v1->v2 migration).
Editing a contract or manifest whose names are already in v2 form and are not being renamed.
A task that merely mentions 'migration' or touches manifests/feature files/contracts without any legacy v1 name being migrated.

given: A plan, wagon or acceptance uses a legacy v1 artifact name (no theme, or dots for hierarchy).
when: The planner migrates that name to v2.
then: Rewrite it as theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant — assign a theme, colons between hierarchy levels, dots only before variants — and realign every wagon manifest, feature file, URN, contract file location and $id field that carries it.
prefer: Steps in order: identify names -> determine theme -> identify hierarchy -> separate hierarchy from variants -> update wagon manifests -> update feature files -> update URNs -> reorganize contracts -> update $id fields.
Templates: identifiers:uuid -> commons:identifiers.uuid; ux.foundations.color -> commons:ux:foundations:color; ux.foundations.color.primary -> commons:ux:foundations:color.primary.
avoid: Renaming only the name while manifests, feature files, URNs, contract layout or $id fields keep the old one.
Dots between hierarchy levels, or a colon before a variant.
why: Piecemeal migration leaves URNs, manifests and contract $ids pointing at different identities; one form with colons for hierarchy and dots for variants keeps them consistent.
evidence: Each migrated name has a theme prefix, colons only between hierarchy levels and dots only before variants (e.g. commons:ux:foundations:color.primary).
No wagon manifest, feature file, URN, contract path or $id field still references the legacy v1 name.
Contract files are reorganized to match the new hierarchy and their $id fields are updated consistently with the migrated identity.
verifier_detail: Reference mappings (v1 -> v2): identifiers:uuid -> commons:identifiers.uuid; ux.foundations.color -> commons:ux:foundations:color; ux.foundations.color.primary -> commons:ux:foundations:color.primary.
Term 'migration_step': one step in the v1->v2 artifact-name migration (the nine ordered steps from identify names through update $id fields).

additions.text: Renaming only the name while dependents keep the old one; dots for hierarchy / colon before variants; no theme prefix.
additions.justification: Inverse of the statement's three required moves (assign theme, separate hierarchy from variants, realign URNs/manifests/contracts); stated as anti-patterns, no new obligation.

additions.text: Engineering reason for consistent identities across URNs, manifests and $ids.
additions.justification: Source has no explicit rationale; derived from the statement's realignment requirement.

additions.text: doesNotFire for new names with no legacy predecessor, for renames of already-v2 names, and for keyword/file-kind matches without a legacy v1 name.
additions.justification: Scopes this rule to v1->v2 migration as the source does, and against planner.artifact-naming.naming-pattern, which it follows per graph.json.
